historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case revenue path FY26-FY31: guided volume step-up (405koz -> 525koz) offset by gold normalizing from US$3,693 to US$3,000/oz; the historical CAGRs are price-cycle artefacts, not a growth trend
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 21.5% vs owner-FCF 3yr CAGR -14.8%: divergence far beyond 30%. Both describe the same two things -- a gold price that rose from ~US$1,800 (FY23) to US$3,693 (FY26) and a growth-capex cycle (Nyanzaga + CMA + Bagoe) that absorbed FY26 cash flow. Neither is a forward growth rate.
historical_growth.notes: 3-year CAGRs run FY2023->FY2026, all in USD. 5-year CAGRs run FY2021->FY2026 and cross the AUD->USD reporting switch at FY2023; FY2021 AUD values were converted at the FY21 average AUDUSD ~0.75 (revenue A$679.7m -> US$510m; equity A$1,031.4m -> US$774m; EPS A$0.094 -> US$0.0705; owner FCF A$47.5m -> US$35.6m), so they are approximate. Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - interest income each year (FY23: 292.7 - 2.6 - 6.0 = 284.1; FY26: 197.3 - 2.8 - 18.6 = 175.9). Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (-14.8%) below reported (-12.3%) because interest income on the cash pile tripled; SBC is immaterial.

scenario_narratives.base: The company's own plan at a normalized gold price. FY27 is the transitional year management guided: 420-480koz at AISC US$1,835-2,070 with ~US$530m growth capex (Nyanzaga ~230, CMA ~80, Edikan cutbacks ~140), so owner FCF is near zero despite a US$4,000 realized price. From FY28 Nyanzaga (first gold January 2027, 4.1Moz reserve, 16-year life) and CMA Underground lift the group to the guided 515-535koz, and AISC falls toward -- but not all the way to -- the guided US$1,400-1,500. The valuation's single biggest axis is the gold price: the base does not pay for today's US$4,305 spot, it normalizes to US$3,000 by FY30, which is where the mid-cycle owner FCF of ~US$370-410m/yr comes from. Government free-carries (10-20%) and cash tax are charged together at 30% rising to 35% of EBIT. The terminal is capped at 10x FY36 FCF because reserves support ~13 years at the plateau.
scenario_narratives.bull: Gold stays where it is. Spot US$4,300 holds through FY29 and then inflates 2%/yr, Nyanzaga and CMA deliver at the top of their plans (550koz group from FY29), and AISC reaches management's US$1,400 as Nyanzaga's lower-cost ounces dilute Yaoure's rising strip ratio. On those inputs the FY29+ EBITDA margin is ~68% and owner FCF ~US$0.9-1.0bn/yr; even at a 10x cap this more than doubles the base value. Everything in this case is 'spot holds and the plan works' -- no re-rating and no M&A is assumed.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2012-15 gold cycle repeated onto a higher-cost, more-taxed asset base. Gold falls 44% to US$2,400 by FY30; Perseus is unhedged so it takes the full hit. Nyanzaga is late and over budget (FY27 capex US$640m), the group plateaus at 490koz, and AISC stays ~US$1,700 because Ghanaian and Ivorian royalty regimes that rose in FY26 do not fall back and Edikan/Yaoure grades keep declining. Margins compress to ~30% and owner FCF to ~US$120-130m/yr; the US$0.92bn net cash and US$0.23bn equity portfolio then carry most of the value. A coup, a mining-code rewrite or a Tanzanian free-carry increase would sit inside this case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value a gold miner on mid-cycle owner cash flow, not on the price the metal happens to trade at today. FY26's record profit was a gold-price event (realized US$3,693 vs 2,543, +45%) on falling grades and rising costs; FY27 is a guided transitional year in which ~US$530m of growth capex absorbs nearly all cash flow. The base case therefore pays for the guided volume step-up to ~525koz at a US$3,000/oz gold price and a US$1,470-1,500 AISC, charges government free-carries and tax together, adds the US$0.92bn net cash and the US$0.23bn listed equity portfolio, deducts the declared-but-unpaid final dividend, and caps the terminal at 10x because reserves are finite. The bull case is what the stock is currently priced for; the gap between the base and the price is the premium the market pays for spot gold persisting.
key_risks_to_valuation: Gold price: every US$100/oz on the mid-cycle deck moves base owner FCF by ~US$35-40m/yr (roughly A$0.30-0.35/share of value at 10x); the base US$3,000 deck is a judgment, not a forecast

Nyanzaga execution: 67% complete at 30 June 2026 against a US$523m budget with first gold January 2027 -- a six-month slip or 20% overrun shifts ~US$100m of FCF and delays the 525koz plateau by a year

Royalty and tax regimes: Ghana and Cote d'Ivoire lifted royalties in FY26; the combined 35% tax + free-carry leakage assumed from FY30 could rise under new mining codes (Tanzania's 20% free-carry is already the highest)

Reserve depletion and grade: Yaoure head grade fell from 2.10 to 1.39 g/t and Edikan from 0.97 to 0.77 g/t in FY26; the 10x terminal cap and 485koz taper assume reserves are replaced at roughly the current pace
Capital allocation: the failed A$2.1bn Predictive Discovery bid shows appetite for large scrip M&A; a dilutive deal is not in any scenario
FX: the AUD quote moves with AUDUSD (0.7016 used); a 5c move in AUDUSD shifts the AUD value by ~7% with no change in the USD valuation

SBC is 0.19% of revenue -- effectively an SBC-zero filer, kept explicit at 0.2%.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and all flows are USD (Perseus switched from AUD to USD reporting at FY2023; the Metrics.csv Currency column is AUD for FY2016-H1 FY2023 and USD from FY2023). ASX quote is AUD. fx_rate is USD->AUD = 1/0.7016 = 1.4253 (Yahoo AUDUSD=X, 2026-09-25T04:12Z). Parity check against the TSX dual listing: PRU.TO C$6.53 (prior TSX close) x CADUSD 0.7068 = US$4.62 vs PRU.AX A$6.635 x 0.7016 = US$4.66, a 0.9% gap on an eight-hour-older print -- rate, direction and quote basis confirmed. Dividends are declared in A$ cents (FY26 final 9.0 A-cents).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T04:11:25Z ASX mid-session (regular trading, not after-hours); 52-week range 4.42-6.96
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,327,131,493 ordinary shares on issue at 30 June 2026 (FY26 AR note 13 -- the Metrics.csv 1,358.2m is the WEIGHTED diluted average for the year, not the closing count, because the A$126.7m FY26 buyback cancelled 28.9m shares) plus ~8.7m dilutive performance rights (diluted 1,358.16m less basic weighted 1,349.45m) less 3.0m rights that lapsed in July 2026 = ~1,333m fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. Buybacks (US$100.0m FY26, A$150m programme ~A$23m unspent at 30 June) are value-neutral in this model and merely fund the flat count.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in USD, the currency of the flows: US 10-year ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.0 = ~9.2% cost of equity, plus ~1pp for concentrated Ghana / Cote d'Ivoire / Tanzania sovereign, royalty-regime and security exposure = 10.0%. No borrowings (US$400m facility undrawn), so WACC = cost of equity. Risk is charged ONCE: gold-price cyclicality lives in the three scenario paths, jurisdiction in the discount rate; the same 10% is used for all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt: lease liabilities US$2.1m (0.7 current + 1.4 non-current) are the only debt and sit in net debt; no lease charge in the flows. Immaterial either way.
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows: government free-carried interests (Ghana 10% Edikan; Cote d'Ivoire 10% Sissingue/Bagoe/Yaoure plus 4% local at Sissingue; Tanzania 20% Nyanzaga) are folded into the cash_tax_rate_path as a combined tax + NCI leakage rate on EBIT (30% FY27 rising to 35% as Nyanzaga's 20% free-carry starts contributing). The NCI equity stock (US$163.7m at 30 June 2026) is NOT deducted in the bridge -- charging it there as well would count the minority twice. Calibration: FY26 EBIT (clean EBITDA ~807 less D&A 117 = ~690) x (1 - 0.30) = ~483 vs reported attributable profit 428 + (book tax 235 - cash tax 163 deferred) = ~501 on a cash basis; ties within non-operating noise (FX loss 34, disposal gain 22).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical') with owner-fcf-adaptations applied: dual currency (a2), leases (b), NCI (c), matching-asset rule (d), near-SBC-zero (e), risk charged once (f). Fresh build, no prior DCF. WHY THIS MODEL: a producing, dividend-paying, net-cash gold miner with three operating mines and a fourth in construction is an operating company whose value is its owner-FCF stream; the cyclical adaptation is that FY2026 is NOT extrapolated -- revenue and margins are rebuilt bottom-up from ounces x realized gold price x AISC, with the gold price normalized from the FY26 realized US$3,693/oz (spot US$4,305 on 2026-09-25, 52-week range 3,764-5,586) to a mid-cycle US$3,000/oz by FY30 in the base case. EBITDA ANCHOR: the stored FY26 EBITDA of 844.7 = PBT + D&A + borrowing costs and therefore includes interest income 18.6 and the Meyas Sand disposal gain 21.9; the US$89.6m fair-value gain on equity investments is in OCI, not PBT. Clean operating EBITDA before SBC = gross profit pre-D&A 860.5 + other income ex interest 9.6 - other expenses 4.9 - corporate 24.1 - FX loss 34.0 = ~807 (54.4% margin); the driver paths are built from per-ounce economics (EBITDA = oz x (price - (AISC - ~US$100/oz sustaining capital)) - ~US$40m corporate/other growing 3%/yr), not from that margin carried forward. CAPEX: FY27 ~US$615m = guided ~530 growth (Nyanzaga completion ~230, CMA Underground ~80, Edikan Fetish/Esuajah North cutbacks ~140) + ~45 sustaining + ~40 exploration; from FY28 growth capex falls away and ~US$190-220m/yr covers sustaining, cutbacks/deferred stripping and exploration (history ex-build years: US$120-210m on 400-500koz). Sustaining capital is excluded from the EBITDA cost so it is charged once, in capex. D&A rises from 7.8% to ~13.6% of revenue as Nyanzaga (US$523m + acquisition cost) and CMA depreciate on units of production. TAX: cash tax lagged book in FY26 (22.7% vs 32.9% of PBT) on capital allowances; the path ramps the combined tax + NCI leakage from 30% to 35%. WORKING CAPITAL: receivables + inventory (bullion, GIC, stockpiles US$395m) exceed payables, so capture is -3% of the revenue change (growth consumes cash, falling revenue releases it). BULLION on hand (27,299oz, US$37.2m at cost) is normal working stock and is not added to the bridge. Interest income (US$18.6m) stripped because net cash US$922m is ~5x the owner-FCF base. TERMINAL: 10x cap (below the 12-15x cyclical default) because P&P reserves of 7.0Moz at ~525koz/yr are ~13 years, so the terminal at FY36 capitalises a mine plan with 3-4 reserve years plus 10.6Moz M&I and exploration; production tapers from 525koz to 485koz over FY32-36 to encode depletion. Weighted IV, entry prices and required-return rows are USD-built and converted to AUD at fx_rate; unsuffixed values are in the AUD quote currency.

gold_price_deck.note: FY27-FY36 realized US$/oz. Base normalizes to US$3,000 mid-cycle by FY30 (~30% below spot, ~19% below FY26 realized) then +1.5%/yr nominal; bull holds spot flat to FY29 then +2%/yr; bear is a 2013-style bust to US$2,400 by FY30 then +1.5%/yr.

aisc_usd_oz.note: Base FY28-31 sits ~US$100/oz above the level implied by management's five-year 1,400-1,500 average (which must average ~1,325 in FY28-31 to absorb the FY27 transitional year) -- deliberate: Perseus's AISC has crept above guidance before, royalty regimes in Ghana and Cote d'Ivoire rose in FY26, and 2% cost inflation is applied from FY30. Royalty relief from the lower base gold price partly offsets.

bear.narrative: A 2013-style gold bust: US$3,600 FY27 falling to US$2,400 by FY30 (-44% from spot); 425koz FY27 (bottom of guidance) and Nyanzaga ramps slowly to a 490koz group plateau; AISC at the top of FY27 guidance (US$2,070) and only reaches US$1,680 as royalty regimes ratchet and grades at Edikan/Yaoure keep falling; FY27 capex US$640m on a Nyanzaga overrun; production tapers to 445koz by FY36.

base.narrative: 450koz FY27 (guidance midpoint) at US$4,000/oz and AISC US$1,950 (guidance midpoint) with ~US$615m capex as Nyanzaga is completed; 520-525koz from FY28 as Nyanzaga (first gold Jan 2027) and CMA Underground reach steady state; gold normalizes to US$3,000 mid-cycle by FY30; AISC settles at US$1,470-1,500 then inflates 2%/yr; production tapers to 485koz by FY36 for depletion.

bull.narrative: Gold holds today's US$4,300 spot through FY29 then compounds 2%/yr; 470koz FY27 (top of guidance), 550koz from FY29 as Nyanzaga outperforms its 200koz+ plan; AISC hits management's US$1,400 by FY29 as royalties and grade normalize; capex ~US$180-210m/yr after FY27.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 10x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 rather than the 15/50/35 house default. Bull raised to only 25% (not 35%) because the bull case is 'spot gold holds at a level 2.1x its FY23 average', which is the market's central expectation but a single-variable bet that needs no operational upside -- the house view is that a price 30% above our mid-cycle is not the base. Bear raised to 25% because Perseus is unhedged, single-commodity, and concentrated in three jurisdictions that raised royalties in FY26 and carry coup/mining-code risk; a 2013-style 40%+ gold drawdown has happened within the operating lives of these mines. No going-concern or covenant risk (no debt, US$0.92bn net cash) keeps bear from going higher.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
